authority: jsonata.org, $string: "Numeric infinity and NaN throw an error because they cannot be represented as a JSON number" — one of the four documented casting rules, and one of the few places the documentation makes a builtin throw on a value rather than a type. The documentation names no code — it publishes no error-code page at all (docs/behaviors.md 2.0) — so the code spelling is jsntrs' own: D3001 for a bare non-finite number, D1001 for a composite that contains one. That split is inherited vocabulary recorded in docs/behaviors.md 1.3, not a documented rule; the throw is what this case pins.
